{{short description|On angles formed when a sphere is inscribed within a tetrahedron}}
[[File:Bang s theoremtetrahedra.png|thumb|500px|right]]
In [[geometry]], '''Bang's theorem on tetrahedra''' states that, if a [[sphere]] is [[inscribed sphere|inscribed]] within a [[tetrahedron]], and segments are drawn from the points of tangency to each vertex on the same face of the tetrahedron, then all four points of tangency have the same triple of angles. In particular, it follows that the 12 triangles into which the segments subdivide the faces of the tetrahedron form congruent pairs across each edge of the tetrahedron.<ref name="brown">{{citation|last=Brown|first=B. H.|title=Theorem of Bang. Isosceles tetrahedra|journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]]|date=April 1926|pages=224–226|volume=33|issue=4|jstor= 2299548|department=Undergraduate Mathematics Clubs: Club Topics|doi=10.1080/00029890.1926.11986564 }}.</ref> It is named after Alfred Sophus Bang, who posed it as a problem in 1897.<ref>{{citation|title=Opgaver til Løsning|journal=Nyt Tidsskrift for Matematik|volume=8|issue=A|year=1897|page=48|language=Danish|jstor= 24528123}}, problem 266.</ref>
